description:
Laurel is on a mission to return time. As the leading AI Time platform for professional services firms, we’re transforming how organizations capture, analyze, and optimize their most valuable resource: time. Our proprietary machine learning technology automates work time capture and connects time data to business outcomes, enabling firms to increase profitability, improve client delivery, and make data-driven strategic decisions. We serve many of the world's largest accounting and law firms, including EY, Aprio, Crowell & Moring, and Frost Brown Todd, and process over 1 billion work activities annually that have never been collected and aggregated before Laurel’s AI Time platform.

Our team comprises top talent in AI, product development, and engineering—innovative, humble, and forward-thinking professionals committed to redefining productivity in the knowledge economy. We're building solutions that empower workers to deliver twice the value in half the time, giving people more time to be creative and impactful. If you're passionate about transforming how people work and building a lasting company that explores the essence of time itself, we'd love to meet you.

The Opportunity

This role starts with legal operations. You will own the function: the templates, playbooks, workflows, tooling, and metrics that let Laurel's legal team support a company that is growing fast, and the steady stream of improvements that make legal easier for the rest of the organization to work with. Laurel already runs on Ironclad, integrated with Salesforce. What we do not yet have is the full build-out for the legal function. That build-out is yours.

If you own how legal work gets done, it follows that you will have a meaningful understanding of the day-to-day. You will work on Laurel's high-volume commercial work: order forms, standard customer edits, NDAs, and the questions that come with them from Go To Market. This is not a role built around marquee negotiations. It is built around the hundred small things that come across a legal team's desk every week, most of which look a lot like the last hundred. You will be the person who handles them quickly, consistently, and well, and who recognizes when something is not routine and brings in the right people rather than forcing it through.

Here is the part that matters most. Most people who work on legal automation will tell you that 80 percent of what a legal team does can be made repeatable and the other 20 percent needs a lawyer every time. We think 80/20 is a starting point, not a ceiling. The 20 percent is not a pile of one-off questions. It is a set of patterns. Your job is to find the pattern, get one clear answer, turn that answer into a rule, and build the rule into the playbook and the tooling so the same question never needs manual intervention again. Do that over and over and 80/20 becomes 90/10, then 95/5. If you are the kind of person who gets a little annoyed every time you have to do the same thing twice, this role was written for you.

Most legal operations roles are built for people who do not practice law. Most junior counsel roles keep you inside the four corners of the contract. This role is intentionally a blend of both. We want someone with legal chops who wants to get into the legal issues, not someone who wants to stay on the operations side of the line, whether you come to this from a law firm, an in-house team, or a legal operations seat. We believe the people who will lead legal functions in five years are the ones who understand the work well enough to do it and well enough to redesign it.

This role reports to Laurel's Associate General Counsel, Commercial and Revenue, and works in close partnership cross-functionally day to day. The legal side of the role is designed to grow: you will start with the repeatable work, and as you demonstrate judgment you will take on more of the substantive questions sitting behind it.

We are looking for someone who wants to help us answer questions such as:

  • What does a commercial contracting process look like when the standard case never touches a lawyer?

  • How do you take a legal process from 80 percent repeatable to 95, and what has to be true to get there?

  • How does a small legal team support a company that is quickly growing in size?

We are not hiring you because you already know how to do all of this. We are hiring you because you are excited enough to learn, work hard, and make a meaningful impact.

What You'll Do

Legal Operations & Systems

This is where you build, and it is the priority. You will own the systems that let a small legal team support a growing company:

  • Owning Ironclad administration: workflow design, templates, approval routing, conditional logic, and reporting, and partnering with Revenue on the Salesforce integration

  • Building and maintaining the commercial playbook, template library, fallback positions, and clause bank, and encoding them into the tooling so the business can self-serve

  • Developing AI-enabled workflows for first-pass review of customer edits, redline summaries, obligation extraction, and knowledge retrieval

  • Working the exceptions: tracking what still escalates to an attorney, finding the patterns in it, getting the legal call made once, and operationalizing that answer as a playbook rule, a template change, or a workflow so it stops escalating

  • Defining and tracking legal team metrics: turnaround time, volume, where deals stall, and where legal time actually goes

  • Building and maintaining the legal knowledge base, FAQs, and training materials so routine questions get answered without a lawyer

  • Evaluating emerging legal technology and AI tools and recommending what Laurel should adopt next

Commercial & Transactional

You will work on the repeatable commercial work that keeps deals moving, and you will be the one making it more repeatable. Responsibilities include:

  • Owning the order form process end to end: preparing, reviewing, routing for approval, and getting to signature

  • Handling common customer-requested edits to Laurel's standard terms against the playbook, and escalating anything outside it with a recommendation

  • Running the NDA pipeline

  • Serving as the first point of contact for commercial legal questions from Sales and Finance

  • Keeping executed agreements, obligations, and renewals organized, accurate, and findable in Ironclad

  • Supporting the legal team on larger negotiations as needed

Strategic Projects

You will regularly work on projects beyond a traditional contracts desk. Examples may include:

  • Cross-functional projects where Legal can serve as a model for AI adoption across the company

  • Internal operational improvements for Sales, Finance, and Legal handoffs

  • Projects that put Laurel's own product to work inside the legal function

At Laurel, Legal is expected to be a force multiplier for the business, not only a review function.

What We're Looking For

You may currently be:

  • An early-career in-house attorney at a SaaS company who has lived inside a CLM and knows what it could be

  • A first- to third-year associate in a commercial, technology transactions, or corporate practice

  • A J.D. who has been working in legal operations, contracts management, or CLM administration and wants a seat closer to the legal work

  • More important than your current title is your trajectory.

You likely possess:

  • 1 to 3 years of experience with commercial contracts, whether at a law firm, in-house, or in a legal operations or contracts seat

  • Admitted to practice in a U.S. jurisdiction

  • Strong drafting fundamentals, the judgment to know what matters in a deal and what does not, and a real appetite for the legal issues behind the contracts

  • A systems mindset: you notice when the same problem keeps showing up and want to fix the process, not just the instance

  • Comfort with technology and a demonstrated interest in AI tools, whether or not you have formal technical training

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, especially with non-lawyers

  • Strong project management and organizational habits

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and a bias toward action

  • High ownership and personal accountability

Bonus points for:

  • Ironclad administration experience, or hands-on experience with another CLM

  • Familiarity with Salesforce and how contracts flow from quote to signature to invoice

  • Experience building prompts, workflows, or automations, in any context

  • Experience with SaaS order forms and standard customer edit requests

  • Experience working with or selling to law firms or accounting firms

  • Familiarity with information security and privacy as they come up in contracting, such as security questionnaires and DPAs

  • An IAPP certification (CIPP or similar) or another privacy or security credential

  • Startup or founder-led company experience

How You Work

You are a builder. You enjoy figuring things out before someone hands you a playbook, and then you write the playbook so the next person does not have to.

You think like a lawyer. You take the contract seriously, you know the difference between a real risk and a theoretical one, and you protect the company without slowing it down.

You prefer creating systems over repeatedly solving the same problem.

You learn quickly and seek responsibility. You are energized by difficult problems and comfortable being uncomfortable.

You are willing to question assumptions, including your own.

You care more about learning velocity than credentials.

You believe technology will fundamentally reshape legal work and want to help lead that transformation.

You are excited about learning through proximity, feedback, and direct collaboration. You see working closely with experienced operators as an accelerant to your own development.

What Success Looks Like After 12 Months

By the end of your first year, you will have:

  • Taken ownership of Laurel's commercial playbook, templates, and fallback positions, and encoded them into Ironclad so the standard case never waits on a lawyer

  • Rebuilt Laurel's Ironclad workflows so that the business can self-serve the majority of order forms and NDAs

  • Built and deployed AI-enabled workflows that measurably cut turnaround time and legal hours per deal

  • Moved the needle on the 20 percent: measurably reduced the share of order forms and customer edits that need an individual attorney, by turning recurring exceptions into playbook rules and automation

  • Established a set of legal metrics that leadership looks at and that drive decisions

  • Helped establish Laurel as a model for what an AI-native legal function can look like

Most importantly, you will have developed capabilities that very few legal professionals possess today: the ability to do the legal work well, to design the systems that work gets done in, and to use AI to do both.

Who This Role Is Not For

This role is probably not the right fit if:

  • You are primarily seeking a traditional in-house commercial role built around negotiations

  • You want to do legal operations without touching the legal work, or the legal work without touching operations

  • You think "that part is just manual" is an acceptable final answer

  • You prefer highly structured environments with clearly defined responsibilities

  • You are uncomfortable experimenting with new technologies

  • You view AI as a threat rather than an opportunity

  • You are looking for predictable work and limited ambiguity

Why Laurel

Most companies are trying to figure out how AI fits into their workflows. We are trying to redesign the workflows themselves. We believe the legal function should be one of the first places that transformation happens, and we sell to the law firms and accounting firms who are asking the same questions.

If you are excited by the idea of doing the legal work and building the function at the same time, while developing into a highly leveraged, business-minded legal professional, we might have a spot for you.

What Laurel is

Laurel is building the system of record for human and agentic work.

The trust Laurel has built with regulated enterprises—and, even more importantly, their end-users— has enabled it to be the first company ever to deploy a multimodal desktop agent at scale (45K+ professionals and 70+ countries). This enables Laurel to collect work that no one else has.

 

Half of enterprise work happens in systems with no API or OS-level access which no tech—other than a multimodal desktop agent—can capture.

Laurel collects more than just metadata; it captures the work itself. And to make the data useful, Laurel builds workflows that requires the professional who did the work to label it accurately, creating a reinforcement learning flywheel that nobody else in the world has.

The result is +2B (and counting) of human-verified labels, creating what is becoming the world’s largest repository of last-mile enterprise data and workflows.

 

How Laurel did it

Laurel developed its data infrastructure by creating the AI Billing category in professional services (legal, accounting, consulting). Laurel earned the trust of the enterprise (in the form of +$1B in profit returned) and end-users (in the form of 1.53M work hours returned) to collect all digital work, even work happening in digital systems that were previously invisible to AI.

 

Laurel is now re-running the same playbook in financial services (insurance, banks, private equity, etc). Same data infrastructure. But instead of billing, it is creating the Work Observability category to expand its feedback loop.

 

What’s next

Packaging its last-mile data in the form of:

  • Post-training: an open-source model on Laurel’s data improved performance by 33%, matching the frontier, at 1% of the cost.

  • Context: Feeding this data into a frontier model’s context window improves task automation by 21%.

  • This is how Laurel accelerates its growth from 4x YoY (current) to +10x YoY).
